---
title: "Multivariate LSTM Stock Forecasting with quantmod and keras3"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
    code_folding: show
params:
  target: "Close"
  tickers: "TSLA"
  horizon: 20
  run_pipeline: true
---

This notebook is the R equivalent of `run_yfinance_lstm.py`. It accepts Yahoo
Finance symbols for stocks, commodities, currencies, and similar instruments;
downloads a rolling five-year daily price history; creates chronological
training, validation, and test sets; trains a multivariate LSTM; and keeps its
outcomes and evaluation results in R data frames.

The configured ticker run executes when the document is knitted. To inspect the
notebook without downloading data or training models, set `run_pipeline` to
`false`. To run it programmatically, use:

```r
rmarkdown::render(
  "LSTM.Rmd",
  params = list(run_pipeline = TRUE)
)
```

The `LSTM_TARGET` environment variable, when set, overrides the `target`
parameter. Supported targets are `Open`, `Close`, `High`, and `Low`.

```{r directories_and_features, include=FALSE}
PROJECT_ROOT <- normalizePath(".", mustWork = TRUE)
MODEL_DIR <- file.path(PROJECT_ROOT, "models", "R_lstm")
dir.create(MODEL_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

FEATURES <- c("Open", "High", "Low", "Close", "Adj Close", "Volume")
TARGETS <- c("Open", "Close", "High", "Low")
LOOKBACK <- 60L
SEED <- 42L
```

## Data and preprocessing helpers

```{r data-helpers}
validate_target <- function(target) {
  if (length(target) != 1L || is.na(target) || !target %in% TARGETS) {
    stop(
      sprintf(
        "target must be one of %s; received %s",
        paste(TARGETS, collapse = ", "),
        deparse(target)
      ),
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
  target
}

download_data <- function(ticker, end = Sys.Date() + 1L) {
  start <- seq.Date(as.Date(end), by = "-5 years", length.out = 2L)[2L]
  prices <- quantmod::getSymbols(
    ticker,
    src = "yahoo",
    from = start,
    to = as.Date(end),
    auto.assign = FALSE,
    warnings = FALSE
  )

  frame <- data.frame(
    Date = as.Date(zoo::index(prices)),
    Open = as.numeric(quantmod::Op(prices)),
    High = as.numeric(quantmod::Hi(prices)),
    Low = as.numeric(quantmod::Lo(prices)),
    Close = as.numeric(quantmod::Cl(prices)),
    `Adj Close` = as.numeric(quantmod::Ad(prices)),
    Volume = as.numeric(quantmod::Vo(prices)),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  frame <- frame[stats::complete.cases(frame), c("Date", FEATURES), drop = FALSE]
  frame <- frame[order(frame$Date), , drop = FALSE]
  rownames(frame) <- NULL

  if (nrow(frame) == 0L) {
    stop(sprintf("No data returned for %s", ticker), call. = FALSE)
  }
  frame
}

construct_lstm_data <- function(data, sequence_size, target_idx) {
  data <- as.matrix(data)
  storage.mode(data) <- "double"
  sequence_size <- as.integer(sequence_size)
  target_idx <- as.integer(target_idx)

  if (sequence_size < 1L) {
    stop("sequence_size must be at least 1", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (target_idx < 1L || target_idx > ncol(data)) {
    stop("target_idx is outside the feature columns", call. = FALSE)
  }

  sample_count <- nrow(data) - sequence_size
  if (sample_count <= 0L) {
    return(list(
      x = array(numeric(), dim = c(0L, sequence_size, ncol(data))),
      y = numeric()
    ))
  }

  x <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(sample_count, sequence_size, ncol(data)))
  y <- numeric(sample_count)
  for (i in seq_len(sample_count)) {
    x[i, , ] <- data[i:(i + sequence_size - 1L), , drop = FALSE]
    y[[i]] <- data[i + sequence_size, target_idx]
  }
  list(x = x, y = y)
}

fit_minmax_scaler <- function(data) {
  data <- as.matrix(data)
  storage.mode(data) <- "double"
  data_min <- apply(data, 2L, min)
  data_max <- apply(data, 2L, max)
  data_range <- data_max - data_min
  data_range[data_range == 0] <- 1

  structure(
    list(
      data_min = data_min,
      data_range = data_range,
      feature_names = colnames(data)
    ),
    class = "lstm_minmax_scaler"
  )
}

transform_minmax <- function(data, scaler) {
  data <- as.matrix(data)
  storage.mode(data) <- "double"
  if (ncol(data) != length(scaler$data_min)) {
    stop("data and scaler must have the same number of features", call. = FALSE)
  }
  sweep(sweep(data, 2L, scaler$data_min, FUN = "-"),
    2L, scaler$data_range, FUN = "/"
  )
}

inverse_target <- function(values, scaler, target_idx) {
  target_idx <- as.integer(target_idx)
  if (target_idx < 1L || target_idx > length(scaler$data_min)) {
    stop("target_idx is outside the scaler features", call. = FALSE)
  }
  as.numeric(values) * scaler$data_range[[target_idx]] + scaler$data_min[[target_idx]]
}

prepare_lstm_data <- function(data, target, lookback = LOOKBACK) {
  target <- validate_target(target)
  lookback <- as.integer(lookback)
  missing_features <- setdiff(FEATURES, names(data))
  if (length(missing_features) > 0L) {
    stop(
      "data is missing feature columns: ",
      paste(missing_features, collapse = ", "),
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  n <- nrow(data)
  train_end <- floor(n * 0.70)
  validate_end <- floor(n * 0.85)
  if (train_end <= lookback || validate_end <= train_end || validate_end >= n) {
    stop("data does not contain enough rows for the requested splits and lookback", call. = FALSE)
  }

  train_rows <- seq_len(train_end)
  validate_rows <- seq.int(train_end + 1L, validate_end)
  test_rows <- seq.int(validate_end + 1L, n)
  target_idx <- match(target, FEATURES)

  scaler <- fit_minmax_scaler(data[train_rows, FEATURES, drop = FALSE])
  all_scaled <- transform_minmax(data[, FEATURES, drop = FALSE], scaler)

  train_sequences <- construct_lstm_data(
    all_scaled[train_rows, , drop = FALSE], lookback, target_idx
  )
  validate_context <- seq.int(train_end - lookback + 1L, validate_end)
  validate_sequences <- construct_lstm_data(
    all_scaled[validate_context, , drop = FALSE], lookback, target_idx
  )
  test_context <- seq.int(validate_end - lookback + 1L, n)
  test_sequences <- construct_lstm_data(
    all_scaled[test_context, , drop = FALSE], lookback, target_idx
  )

  list(
    scaler = scaler,
    target_idx = target_idx,
    split_rows = list(
      train = train_rows,
      validate = validate_rows,
      test = test_rows
    ),
    train = c(train_sequences, list(dates = data$Date[(lookback + 1L):train_end])),
    validate = c(validate_sequences, list(dates = data$Date[validate_rows])),
    test = c(test_sequences, list(dates = data$Date[test_rows]))
  )
}

build_outcome_frames <- function(predictions, ticker, target) {
  split_names <- intersect(c("train", "validate", "test"), names(predictions))
  actual_rows <- lapply(split_names, function(split_name) {
    item <- predictions[[split_name]]
    data.frame(
      ticker = ticker,
      target = target,
      split = split_name,
      Date = as.Date(item$dates),
      actual = as.numeric(item$actual),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
  predicted_rows <- lapply(split_names, function(split_name) {
    item <- predictions[[split_name]]
    data.frame(
      ticker = ticker,
      target = target,
      split = split_name,
      Date = as.Date(item$dates),
      predicted = as.numeric(item$predicted),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })

  list(
    actual_outcomes = do.call(rbind, actual_rows),
    predicted_outcomes = do.call(rbind, predicted_rows)
  )
}
```

## Model construction

The architecture matches the Python implementation: four 100-unit LSTM
layers, a 20% dropout layer after each LSTM, and a one-unit dense output.

```{r model-helper}
build_model <- function(input_shape) {
  model <- keras3::keras_model_sequential(input_shape = as.integer(input_shape)) |>
    keras3::layer_lstm(units = 100L, return_sequences = TRUE) |>
    keras3::layer_dropout(rate = 0.2) |>
    keras3::layer_lstm(units = 100L, return_sequences = TRUE) |>
    keras3::layer_dropout(rate = 0.2) |>
    keras3::layer_lstm(units = 100L, return_sequences = TRUE) |>
    keras3::layer_dropout(rate = 0.2) |>
    keras3::layer_lstm(units = 100L, return_sequences = FALSE) |>
    keras3::layer_dropout(rate = 0.2) |>
    keras3::layer_dense(units = 1L)

  model |> keras3::compile(
    optimizer = "adam",
    loss = "mean_squared_error"
  )
  model
}
```

## Recursive forecast helpers

As in the Python version, future values for non-target features are unknown.
The recursive forecast therefore replaces only the selected target with the
model prediction and carries the latest scaled values of the other features
forward. This is a scenario forecast rather than a complete market simulator.

```{r forecast-helpers}
business_days <- function(last_date, horizon) {
  horizon <- as.integer(horizon)
  if (horizon < 0L) {
    stop("horizon cannot be negative", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (horizon == 0L) {
    return(as.Date(character()))
  }

  candidate_count <- ceiling(horizon * 7 / 5) + 7L
  candidates <- seq.Date(
    as.Date(last_date) + 1L,
    by = "day",
    length.out = candidate_count
  )
  weekday_number <- as.POSIXlt(candidates)$wday
  candidates[!weekday_number %in% c(0L, 6L)][seq_len(horizon)]
}

forecast_future <- function(model, recent_data, scaler, target, horizon,
                            lookback = LOOKBACK) {
  target <- validate_target(target)
  lookback <- as.integer(lookback)
  horizon <- as.integer(horizon)
  if (nrow(recent_data) < lookback) {
    stop(
      sprintf("recent_data must contain at least %d rows", lookback),
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
  if (horizon < 1L) {
    stop("horizon must be at least 1", call. = FALSE)
  }

  target_idx <- match(target, FEATURES)
  values <- as.matrix(tail(recent_data[, FEATURES, drop = FALSE], lookback))
  scaled <- transform_minmax(values, scaler)
  forecasts <- numeric(horizon)

  for (step in seq_len(horizon)) {
    model_input <- array(scaled, dim = c(1L, lookback, length(FEATURES)))
    next_scaled <- as.numeric(stats::predict(model, model_input, verbose = 0))[[1L]]
    next_row <- scaled[nrow(scaled), ]
    next_row[[target_idx]] <- next_scaled
    forecasts[[step]] <- inverse_target(next_scaled, scaler, target_idx)
    scaled <- rbind(scaled[-1L, , drop = FALSE], next_row)
  }

  result <- data.frame(
    Date = business_days(tail(recent_data$Date, 1L), horizon),
    forecast = forecasts,
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  names(result)[[2L]] <- target
  result
}

forecast_ticker <- function(ticker, target, horizon = 20L, history_days = 20L) {
  target <- validate_target(target)
  history_days <- as.integer(history_days)
  model_path <- file.path(
    MODEL_DIR,
    sprintf("%s_%s_lstm.keras", tolower(ticker), tolower(target))
  )
  scaler_path <- file.path(
    MODEL_DIR,
    sprintf("%s_%s_scaler.rds", tolower(ticker), tolower(target))
  )

  model <- keras3::load_model(model_path)
  scaler <- readRDS(scaler_path)
  recent_data <- download_data(ticker)
  forecast <- forecast_future(model, recent_data, scaler, target, horizon)
  history_start <- max(1L, nrow(recent_data) - history_days + 1L)
  history <- recent_data[
    seq.int(history_start, nrow(recent_data)),
    c("Date", target),
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  list(forecast = forecast, history = history)
}
```

## Training, evaluation, and reporting

```{r training-helper}
prediction_metrics <- function(actual, predicted) {
  data.frame(
    rmse = sqrt(mean((actual - predicted)^2)),
    mae = mean(abs(actual - predicted))
  )
}

history_epochs <- function(history) {
  as.integer(length(history$metrics$loss))
}

plot_outcomes <- function(actual_outcomes, predicted_outcomes, ticker, target) {
  actual_outcomes$hover_text <- sprintf(
    paste0(
      "Actual<br>Date: %s<br>", target, ": %.4f<br>Split: %s"
    ),
    format(actual_outcomes$Date, "%Y-%m-%d"),
    actual_outcomes$actual,
    tools::toTitleCase(actual_outcomes$split)
  )
  predicted_outcomes$hover_text <- sprintf(
    paste0(
      "Predicted<br>Date: %s<br>", target, ": %.4f<br>Split: %s"
    ),
    format(predicted_outcomes$Date, "%Y-%m-%d"),
    predicted_outcomes$predicted,
    tools::toTitleCase(predicted_outcomes$split)
  )

  figure <- plotly::plot_ly()
  figure <- plotly::add_lines(
    figure,
    data = actual_outcomes,
    x = ~Date,
    y = ~actual,
    name = "Actual",
    text = ~hover_text,
    hoverinfo = "text",
    line = list(color = "#252525", width = 2),
    inherit = FALSE
  )
  figure <- plotly::add_lines(
    figure,
    data = predicted_outcomes,
    x = ~Date,
    y = ~predicted,
    name = "Predicted",
    text = ~hover_text,
    hoverinfo = "text",
    line = list(color = "#2563EB", width = 2, dash = "dash"),
    inherit = FALSE
  )
  figure <- plotly::layout(
    figure,
    title = list(text = sprintf("%s: actual and predicted %s", ticker, target)),
    xaxis = list(
      title = "Date",
      showgrid = FALSE,
      rangeslider = list(visible = TRUE, thickness = 0.08),
      rangeselector = list(
        buttons = list(
          list(count = 1, label = "1m", step = "month", stepmode = "backward"),
          list(count = 3, label = "3m", step = "month", stepmode = "backward"),
          list(count = 6, label = "6m", step = "month", stepmode = "backward"),
          list(count = 1, label = "1y", step = "year", stepmode = "backward"),
          list(step = "all", label = "All")
        )
      )
    ),
    yaxis = list(title = sprintf("%s value", target), gridcolor = "#E5E7EB"),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.1),
    hovermode = "x unified",
    paper_bgcolor = "white",
    plot_bgcolor = "white"
  )
  plotly::config(
    figure,
    displaylogo = FALSE,
    responsive = TRUE,
    scrollZoom = TRUE
  )
}

plot_forecast <- function(forecast, history, ticker, target) {
  history_df <- data.frame(
    Date = as.Date(history$Date),
    value = as.numeric(history[[target]]),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  forecast_df <- data.frame(
    Date = as.Date(forecast$Date),
    value = as.numeric(forecast[[target]]),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  history_df$hover_text <- sprintf(
    paste0("Actual<br>Date: %s<br>", target, ": %.4f"),
    format(history_df$Date, "%Y-%m-%d"),
    history_df$value
  )
  forecast_df$hover_text <- sprintf(
    paste0("Forecast<br>Date: %s<br>", target, ": %.4f"),
    format(forecast_df$Date, "%Y-%m-%d"),
    forecast_df$value
  )

  figure <- plotly::plot_ly()
  figure <- plotly::add_lines(
    figure,
    data = history_df,
    x = ~Date,
    y = ~value,
    name = "Actual",
    text = ~hover_text,
    hoverinfo = "text",
    line = list(color = "#252525", width = 2),
    inherit = FALSE
  )
  figure <- plotly::add_lines(
    figure,
    data = forecast_df,
    x = ~Date,
    y = ~value,
    name = "Forecast",
    text = ~hover_text,
    hoverinfo = "text",
    line = list(color = "#2563EB", width = 2, dash = "dash"),
    inherit = FALSE
  )
  figure <- plotly::layout(
    figure,
    title = list(text = sprintf("%s: recent and forecast %s", ticker, target)),
    xaxis = list(title = "Date", showgrid = FALSE),
    yaxis = list(title = sprintf("%s value", target), gridcolor = "#E5E7EB"),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.1),
    hovermode = "x unified",
    paper_bgcolor = "white",
    plot_bgcolor = "white"
  )
  plotly::config(
    figure,
    displaylogo = FALSE,
    responsive = TRUE,
    scrollZoom = TRUE
  )
}

run_ticker <- function(ticker, target) {
  target <- validate_target(target)
  set.seed(SEED)
  keras3::set_random_seed(SEED)

  data <- download_data(ticker)
  # Expose each ticker's full price history in the global environment so it can
  # be inspected from RStudio's Environment/Data tab.
  assign(ticker, data, envir = globalenv())

  prepared <- prepare_lstm_data(data, target, LOOKBACK)
  scaler_path <- file.path(
    MODEL_DIR,
    sprintf("%s_%s_scaler.rds", tolower(ticker), tolower(target))
  )
  saveRDS(prepared$scaler, scaler_path)

  model <- build_model(c(LOOKBACK, length(FEATURES)))
  model_path <- file.path(
    MODEL_DIR,
    sprintf("%s_%s_lstm.keras", tolower(ticker), tolower(target))
  )
  callbacks <- list(
    keras3::callback_model_checkpoint(
      filepath = model_path,
      monitor = "val_loss",
      save_best_only = TRUE,
      mode = "min"
    ),
    keras3::callback_early_stopping(
      monitor = "val_loss",
      patience = 25L,
      restore_best_weights = TRUE
    )
  )
  history <- model |> keras3::fit(
    x = prepared$train$x,
    y = prepared$train$y,
    validation_data = list(prepared$validate$x, prepared$validate$y),
    epochs = 50L,
    batch_size = 64L,
    callbacks = callbacks,
    verbose = 0L
  )

  best_model <- keras3::load_model(model_path)
  predictions <- lapply(
    c("train", "validate", "test"),
    function(split_name) {
      split <- prepared[[split_name]]
      list(
        actual = inverse_target(
          split$y, prepared$scaler, prepared$target_idx
        ),
        predicted = inverse_target(
          as.numeric(stats::predict(best_model, split$x, verbose = 0L)),
          prepared$scaler,
          prepared$target_idx
        ),
        dates = split$dates
      )
    }
  )
  names(predictions) <- c("train", "validate", "test")
  outcomes <- build_outcome_frames(predictions, ticker, target)

  metrics <- data.frame(
    ticker = ticker,
    target = target,
    rows = nrow(data),
    start = format(min(data$Date), "%Y-%m-%d"),
    end = format(max(data$Date), "%Y-%m-%d"),
    train_rows = length(prepared$split_rows$train),
    validate_rows = length(prepared$split_rows$validate),
    test_rows = length(prepared$split_rows$test),
    epochs_run = history_epochs(history),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  for (split_name in names(predictions)) {
    split_metrics <- prediction_metrics(
      predictions[[split_name]]$actual,
      predictions[[split_name]]$predicted
    )
    metrics[[paste0(split_name, "_rmse")]] <- split_metrics$rmse
    metrics[[paste0(split_name, "_mae")]] <- split_metrics$mae
  }

  list(
    metrics = metrics,
    data = data,
    actual_outcomes = outcomes$actual_outcomes,
    predicted_outcomes = outcomes$predicted_outcomes,
    outcome_plot = plot_outcomes(
      outcomes$actual_outcomes,
      outcomes$predicted_outcomes,
      ticker,
      target
    )
  )
}
```

## Execute the pipeline

```{r run-pipeline}
TARGET <- validate_target(Sys.getenv("LSTM_TARGET", unset = params$target))
TICKERS <- trimws(strsplit(params$tickers, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]])
ticker_results <- NULL
ticker_data <- NULL
metrics <- NULL
actual_outcomes <- NULL
predicted_outcomes <- NULL

if (isTRUE(params$run_pipeline)) {
  ticker_results <- setNames(lapply(TICKERS, function(ticker) {
    run_ticker(
      ticker,
      target = TARGET
    )
  }), TICKERS)
  metrics <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ticker_results, `[[`, "metrics"))
  actual_outcomes <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(ticker_results, `[[`, "actual_outcomes")
  )
  predicted_outcomes <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(ticker_results, `[[`, "predicted_outcomes")
  )
  ticker_data <- setNames(lapply(ticker_results, `[[`, "data"), TICKERS)
} else {
  cat("Pipeline execution is disabled. Set `run_pipeline: true` to train the models.")
}
```

The combined `actual_outcomes` and `predicted_outcomes` objects remain available
as data frames in the knitted R session. Each ticker's full downloaded price
history is also assigned to the global environment under its symbol (for
example, `TSLA`) and collected in the `ticker_data` list, so it can be inspected
from RStudio's Environment/Data tab. Results are not exported to CSV files.

### Model metrics

```{r metrics-table}
if (!is.null(metrics)) { metrics }
```

### Interactive outcomes

```{r interactive-plots}
if (!is.null(ticker_results)) {
  plot_sections <- lapply(names(ticker_results), function(ticker) {
    result <- ticker_results[[ticker]]
    htmltools::tagList(
      htmltools::tags$h2(ticker),
      result$outcome_plot
    )
  })
  htmltools::tagList(plot_sections)
}
```

After a model has been trained, generate a recursive forecast for the configured
horizon and plot it against the trailing 20 days of actual prices with:

```{r forecast-example, eval=FALSE}
tsla_forecast <- forecast_ticker(
  "TSLA",
  target = TARGET,
  horizon = params$horizon
)
tsla_forecast$forecast
plot_forecast(
  tsla_forecast$forecast,
  tsla_forecast$history,
  "TSLA",
  TARGET
)
```
